name: Dermalloy-V
description: Dermalloy-V is a flexible nickel-titanium shape-memory alloy woven at the micro-scale with a living dermal tissue layer — BioForge's engineered keratinocyte-fibroblast matrix grown directly onto and into the metal mesh during a co-culture fabrication process. The result is a material that behaves mechanically like a metal fabric but biologically like skin: it can be sutured to host tissue, develops a blood supply through angiogenesis, heals lacerations using the host's own repair mechanisms, and provides sensory feedback through integrated Meissner-corpuscle analogs embedded in the dermal layer. It is the gold standard outer covering for cosmetic and functional prosthetic limbs.
applications: augment exterior finishing for social integration
cost: Φ14,000 per 100cm² panel (standard); Φ30,000–Φ80,000 per full limb sheath (custom-pigmented, sensory-grade)
story_hooks: A Dermalloy-V covered prosthetic limb has been living on a black-market auction block for months — it was harvested from its original owner and the dermal layer is still alive, still healing, still warm, and bidders are disturbed to find it responds to touch.

An undercover operative's Dermalloy-V disguise is failing — the dermal layer is angiogenically integrating with their real tissue faster than anticipated, and removing it now would require surgery that would blow their cover and possibly kill them.

A Tier 5 socialite has commissioned a full-body Dermalloy-V resurfacing for cosmetic reasons — but their immune system is slowly recognizing that some of the dermal layer's cell cultures were sourced from an unconsenting donor, and a bioethics investigator is following the supply chain.
